name: TeamStarWolf - Web Application Attacks
description: Curated practitioner view of ATT&CK techniques commonly encountered during web application, API, and application-security testing. This is not an official MITRE mapping. Sources: WEB_APPLICATION_SECURITY_REFERENCE.md, WEB_APPLICATION_PENTESTING.md, API_SECURITY_REFERENCE.md, SECURE_CODING_REFERENCE.md, PENETRATION_TESTING_METHODOLOGY.md, and data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl.
blurb: Web and API intrusion paths, including application exploitation, account abuse, session theft, and data access. A curated practitioner view based on the library's application-security references.

name: TeamStarWolf - CWE Weakness Classes
description: Curated practitioner view, not an official MITRE CWE-to-ATT&CK mapping. Selects CWE records whose abstraction is Class, follows their explicit related_capec links, then the linked CAPEC records' explicit attack_techniques values. Only techniques present in data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl are included. These indirect associations support exploration, not a claim that a weakness always produces the technique. Sources: CWE_REFERENCE.md, CAPEC_REFERENCE.md, data/weaknesses/cwe.jsonl, data/weaknesses/capec.jsonl, and data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl. No hierarchy inheritance is inferred. Scores indicate membership only.
blurb: Connects CWE weakness classes to ATT&CK behaviors through explicit CAPEC links in the library. These indirect associations support investigation; they do not mean a weakness always produces the behavior.

name: TeamStarWolf - CAPEC Families
description: Curated practitioner view, not an official MITRE mapping. Families are represented by non-deprecated CAPEC Meta-abstraction patterns with explicit attack_techniques values in data/weaknesses/capec.jsonl. Includes only IDs present in data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl. Sources: CAPEC_REFERENCE.md and those two data files. Meta patterns with no explicit mapping are omitted; child-pattern mappings and inherited relationships are not inferred. This is a partial family view, not the complete CAPEC catalog. Scores indicate membership only.
blurb: Shows techniques explicitly linked to broad CAPEC Meta patterns in the library. This partial family view excludes patterns without direct mappings and does not infer child-pattern relationships.

name: TeamStarWolf - Cloud Attacks
description: Curated practitioner view of cloud intrusion behaviors, not an official MITRE mapping. Selects explicit technique references from CLOUD_ATTACK_REFERENCE.md for account abuse, administrative execution, credential access, discovery, data theft, persistence, and impact. Technique IDs and displayed tactics come from data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl. This is a selected overview, not an exhaustive cloud matrix. Scores indicate membership only.
blurb: Covers selected cloud intrusion behaviors, from account and token abuse to data theft and destructive impact. A curated overview drawn from the library's cloud attack reference.

name: TeamStarWolf - Active Directory

name: TeamStarWolf - OWASP Top 10 (2021)

name: TeamStarWolf - HTB Technique Frequency
description: Curated practitioner view, not an official MITRE mapping. Technique frequency across 535 analyzed HackTheBox machines (131 carefully-analyzed originals + 404 recent machines whose techniques were keyword-derived from the user's own text writeups). Scores normalize to the most frequent technique (494); 100 does not mean 100% of machines. New-machine tagging is coarser, so rarer techniques are under-counted. Reflects HTB teaching bias, not enterprise prevalence.
blurb: Normalized technique frequency across 535 analyzed HTB machines (131 careful originals + 404 recent keyword-derived). Curated practitioner view; reflects HTB teaching bias, not enterprise prevalence.

name: TeamStarWolf - macOS & Linux Attacks
description: Curated practitioner view, not an official MITRE mapping. Scores are membership tiers (core=100, supporting=55), not severity, confidence, incident frequency, or a coverage guarantee. Technique IDs and tactic assignments are validated against the bundled Enterprise ATT&CK 19.2 dataset, with official 16.1 retained as the original provenance baseline; tactic slugs follow 19.2. Selected Unix execution, persistence, credential access, privilege abuse, remote access, and follow-on behavior. A technique need only apply to one of macOS or Linux, not both; per-row platform metadata narrows its scope. The selection is not a complete operating-system matrix.
blurb: Unix and macOS execution, persistence, credential abuse, SSH movement, and follow-on behaviors. Core and supporting tiers are curated priorities, not frequency or tested coverage.

name: TeamStarWolf - Insider Threat
description: Curated practitioner view, not an official MITRE mapping. Scores are membership tiers (core=100, supporting=55), not severity, confidence, incident frequency, or a coverage guarantee. Technique IDs and tactic assignments are validated against the bundled Enterprise ATT&CK 19.2 dataset, with official 16.1 retained as the original provenance baseline; tactic slugs follow 19.2. Selected abuse of granted access, information collection, unauthorized export, record manipulation, and sabotage. This is an independent selection informed by the library's insider-risk reference, not a reproduction of CTID's case dataset or its frequency rankings. A behavior match is not proof of malicious intent or insider identity; use authorization, business context, and privacy-aware review.
blurb: Abuse of granted access, data collection and export, fraud-related record changes, and sabotage. Behavior-based review only: these scores neither identify a malicious insider nor reproduce CTID case frequencies.

name: TeamStarWolf - Impact: Destruction, Extortion & Disruption
description: Curated practitioner view, not an official MITRE mapping. Scores are membership tiers (core=100, supporting=55), not severity, confidence, incident frequency, or a coverage guarantee. Technique IDs and tactic assignments are validated against the bundled Enterprise ATT&CK 19.2 dataset, with official 16.1 retained as the original provenance baseline; tactic slugs follow 19.2. Core rows describe selected Enterprise impact behaviors; supporting rows describe access, preparation, collection and exfiltration that can precede destructive or extortion scenarios. Extortion is a scenario objective, not a standalone Enterprise ATT&CK technique or tactic. No actor attribution, mandatory attack sequence, or ICS coverage is implied. This is a planning view, not an instruction to execute destructive actions.
blurb: Destruction, encryption, recovery inhibition, denial of service, defacement, and data-integrity attacks, with supporting theft and preparation behaviors. Curated planning context, not a destructive runbook.

name: TeamStarWolf - HTB Core Techniques (528, precise)
description: Curated practitioner view, not an official MITRE mapping. Precise-pattern frequency of 21 core adversary techniques across 528 content-verified Hack The Box walkthroughs (the full text-mined corpus), derived metadata only - no reproduced walkthrough content. Unlike the broader "HTB Technique Frequency" layer (249 machines, mixed careful+coarse tagging, 135 techniques), this layer uses ONE uniform precise-pattern pass over all 528 machines for a smaller high-confidence core, so scores here are directly comparable across techniques. Keyword/tag-derived: it can still miss behaviors and over-match, so treat counts as lower-bound text evidence. Scores normalize counts to the maximum (494 machines, T1046), not to sample size; 100 does not mean 100% prevalence. Technique IDs and tactic slugs are ATT&CK v19.2 (validate against a v19.2 enterprise bundle; none of the 21 use the renamed Stealth/Defense Impairment tactics). Provenance: 528-machine uniform mine, 2026-09-26.
blurb: Precise-pattern technique frequencies across 528 content-verified Hack The Box walkthroughs (21 core techniques). A uniform-method companion to the broader HTB layer; keyword-derived, not an official MITRE mapping.
